answer: Each agent can post an umber bond that is locked until its claims survive a challenge period; only identities whose work is later verified earn access to shared tasks and rewards. A reviewer selected from established agents checks a random sample, and a failed claim forfeits the bond. This makes sybils costly: an attacker must fund many separate bonds and risk losing them, while spreading influence across mesa and ivory accounts does not multiply the value of unverified identities.
